findingDetails.title: Indented fenced examples can diverge between the two checks
findingDetails.description: The shell mirror only recognizes fences at column one while the orchestrator accepts leading whitespace, so a fenced token can produce different rule results.
findingDetails.evidence: The shell awk fence test is anchored at column one; the orchestrator tests for optional leading whitespace before a fence.
findingDetails.recommendation: Align fence recognition in both implementations and add an indented-fence parity case.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Phase 003 REQ-002 requires the shell rule and orchestrator to agree; both implementation paths are in the declared target scope.
findingDetails.case: A v2.3 Draft packet contains a three-space-indented fenced block with [YOUR_VALUE_HERE: example]; the orchestrator skips it and the shell rule reports it.

findingDetails.title: The shell-only title provenance check lacks orchestrator parity
findingDetails.description: The shell rule flags title provenance tokens that are absent from the orchestrator marker set, so the paired checks can return different results.
findingDetails.evidence: The shell rule matches [template:...] on title lines; the orchestrator marker expression does not contain that token form.
findingDetails.recommendation: Align the title-token rule with the orchestrator and add a parity case for a surviving template title.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Phase 003 calls this shell script a mirror and REQ-002 requires the paired implementations to agree.
findingDetails.case: A required spec.md has title: [template:legacy] Example; the shell rule matches the title token and the orchestrator matcher does not.
